title: Trapping an Unexpected/Unprecedented Hexanuclear Ce(III) Hydrolysis Product with Neutral 4-Amino-1,2,4-triazole

material_class.structural_family: dinuclear Ce(III) complex with η2μ2κ2 4-amino-1,2,4-triazole bridges

synthesis.procedure: 1,2,3-HTriaz (92 mg, 1.332 mmol) and 4-NH2-1,2,4-Triaz (92 mg, 1.094 mmol) were heated uncovered with stirring at 75 °C for 82 min to a clear colorless solution. CeCl3·7H2O (455 mg, 1.221 mmol) was added, giving a colorless viscous solution after ca. 25 min at 75 °C. After 1 h the temperature was raised to 90 °C for ca. 2 h; after 51 min at 90 °C an opaque white pasty mass formed. The capped vial was cooled to ambient temperature, then after ~4 weeks reheated uncovered to 118 °C with stirring for ca. 10 min and slow-cooled. After standing 6–7 months, colorless single crystals of 1 suitable for SCXRD were selected from the clear colorless solution.
solvents: neat azole melt (no added molecular solvent)
synthesis.temperature: 75 °C then 90 °C; reheated 118 °C; crystallization at ambient temperature
synthesis.time: 82 min at 75 °C; ~2 h at 90 °C; ~10 min reheating; 6–7 months standing
synthesis.vessel_or_method: aluminum-foil-covered 1.5-dram vial with Teflon-coated stir bar; sand/oil bath heating
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: slow cooling after heating cycles; crystals selected directly from the vial after long standing

synthesis.procedure: Following a reported IL dehydration, [C2mim]Cl (200 mg, 1.364 mmol) and CeCl3·7H2O (130 mg, 0.349 mmol) were heated with stirring to 110 °C (clear yellow solution within 21 min), held at 100–110 °C for 31 h until water was absent by FT-IR, then heated at 120 °C for 17 h and slow-cooled from 120 °C to 70 °C over 31 min. 4-NH2-1,2,4-Triaz·5-NH2-HTetaz (0.724 g, 4.280 mmol) was added; the open vial was heated to 130 °C (cocrystal dissolved within 20 min) and held 3.3 h (opaque tan, gas evolution). After capping, the mixture was cooled from 130 °C to 96 °C over 2.5 h (white precipitate). The oil bath was held at 80 °C for ca. 2 weeks; crystals of 2 were isolated by separating liquid from solid with a heated pipette.
synthesis.time: 31 h at 100–110 °C; 17 h at 120 °C; 3.3 h at 130 °C; ca. 2 weeks at 80 °C
synthesis.vessel_or_method: 1.5-dram vial, aluminum foil, sand then oil bath, open then capped
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: held at 80 °C for ca. 2 weeks; liquid separated from solid with a heated pipette; crystals used for SCXRD

synthesis.procedure: 4-NH2-1,2,4-Triaz (82 mg, 0.975 mmol) and 1,2,3-HTriaz (209 mg, 3.026 mmol) were heated in an uncapped 1.5-dram vial to 70 °C (ca. 10 min) to a clear colorless solution, then slow-cooled. At ca. 40 °C, Ce(NO3)3·6H2O was added in 20–30 mg portions to saturation, totaling 540 mg (1.244 mmol) over 2 h. The slightly viscous colorless solution was heated at 95 °C for 18 h (highly viscous bubbling yellow solution). Slow cooling gave a gel. After 5.5 weeks at room temperature the gel was reheated with stirring to 120 °C, then held at 80 °C for ca. 3 days without crystallization and cooled. After ca. 8 months standing, numerous single crystals of 3 nucleated in the gel and were examined by SCXRD.
synthesis.temperature: 70 °C melt; additions at ca. 40 °C; 95 °C then 120 °C; hold 80 °C; ambient crystallization
synthesis.time: ca. 10 min melt; 2 h salt additions; 18 h at 95 °C; ca. 3 days at 80 °C; ca. 8 months standing
synthesis.vessel_or_method: 1.5-dram screw-top vial with Teflon-coated stir bar; oil bath
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: gel nucleated crystals after ca. 8 months; crystals selected directly from the vial

material_class.structural_family: hexanuclear Ce(III) oxo/hydroxo/chloro hydrolysis cluster (Ce6O8-related core)

synthesis.procedure: 4-NH2-1,2,4-Triaz·5-NH2-HTetaz was heated to 150 °C to a clear colorless liquid and 591 mg (3.494 mmol) was transferred by heated pipette to a pre-weighed open aluminum-foil-wrapped vial in a sand bath at 120–140 °C. CeCl3·7H2O was added in 40–70 mg increments to a total of 108 mg (0.290 mmol) until the solution turned clear peach with white precipitate. The mixture was held at 140 °C for ca. 4 h, slow-cooled, and after several weeks at room temperature reheated until it melted at 115 °C. Peach liquid and white precipitate were separated into two closed vials and held at 115 °C. After five days the liquid turned dark green with dark green single crystals; the precipitate vial also contained the same dark green square crystals. Both vials were held at 115 °C another week before crystals were removed for SCXRD. Repeated reactions gave small block crystals of low yield confirmed as 4.
synthesis.time: ca. 4 h at 140 °C; several weeks standing; 5 days then 1 week at 115 °C
synthesis.vessel_or_method: open then closed aluminum-foil-wrapped vial with Teflon stir bar; sand bath; heated-pipette separation
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: peach liquid and white precipitate separated; dark green crystals grown at 115 °C from both aliquots
synthesis.yield: low yield (small block crystals; not quantified)

properties.summary: Preliminary EPR (SI) was used only to support Ce(III); no quantitative magnetic or optical measurements are reported in the main text.
